properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 5 at 1:57PM EDT until September 5 at 2:45PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
SVRGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southwestern Catawba County in the Piedmont of North Carolina...
Southern McDowell County in western North Carolina...
Northeastern Rutherford County in western North Carolina...
Northwestern Lincoln County in the Piedmont of North Carolina...
Northwestern Cleveland County in the Piedmont of North Carolina...
Southern Burke County in western North Carolina...

* Until 245 PM EDT.

* At 157 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 11 miles southeast of Morganton to 17 miles
northeast of Forest City to 9 miles southwest of Marion, moving
southeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind
damage to trees and power lines.

* Locations impacted include...
Marion, Belwood, Old Fort, Lawndale, Fallston, Polkville, Casar,
South Mountains State Park, Thermal City, and Cooksville.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Please report damaging winds, hail, or flooding to the National
Weather Service by calling toll free, 1, 800, 2 6 7, 8 1 0 1, or by
posting on our Facebook page, or post it to X using hashtag nwsgsp.
Your message should describe the event and the specific location
where it occurred.
properties.area: Burke, NC; Catawba, NC; Cleveland, NC; Lincoln, NC; McDowell, NC; Rutherford, NC

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued September 5 at 11:52AM MDT until September 5 at 2:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 1152 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain over the South Fork Burn Scar. Between 0.5 and 1.25 inches of
rain have fallen with the heaviest amounts on the northwest side of
the burn scar.  Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact Upper Canyon, Brady
Canyon, and Perk Canyon as well as the Cedar Creek, Eagle Creek and
Rio Ruidoso drainages. Impacts will include but are not limited to
all nearby reservoirs, bridges, culverts and roadways. Impacts to
areas along the Rio Ruidoso may extend downstream of Ruidoso Downs.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms in and around the
South Fork Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flooding of areas in and around the South Fork Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ruidoso, Ruidoso Downs, Alto, Glencoe and Hollywood.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the South Fork Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.

properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 5 at 1:49PM EDT until September 5 at 2:45PM EDT by NWS Raleigh NC
properties.description:
SVRRAH

The National Weather Service in Raleigh has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Western Forsyth County in central North Carolina...
Central Davidson County in central North Carolina...

* Until 245 PM EDT.

* At 148 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm was located over Huntsville,
or near Yadkinville, moving southeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Winston-Salem, Lexington, Clemmons, Bermuda Run, Huntsville,
Linwood, Lewisville, Pfafftown, High Rock Lake, and Arcadia.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 85 between Mile Markers 84 and 95.
Interstate 40 between Mile Markers 182 and 194.
properties.instruction:
Straight line winds can blow down trees, power lines, and damage
mobile homes and other buildings. Seek shelter in a sturdy structure
until the storm has passed. Stay away from windows as flying debris
generated by damaging winds can be deadly.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued September 5 at 1:48PM EDT until September 5 at 2:45PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
SMWAKQ

The National Weather Service in Wakefield has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Chesapeake Bay from Little Creek VA to Cape Henry VA including the
Chesapeake Bay Bridge Tunnel...
Chesapeake Bay from New Point Comfort to Little Creek VA...
Coastal Waters from Cape Charles Light to Virginia-North Carolina
border out 20 NM...
James River from JRB to HRBT, Including the Elizabeth River...

* Until 245 PM EDT.

* At 148 PM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located 7 nm west of
Poquoson, moving southeast at 35 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Chesapeake Bay Bridge Tunnel, 1st Island Bay Bridge, Anglo African
Wreck, Virginia Beach Oceanfront, Cape Henry, Thimble Shoals,
Hampton Roads Bridge Tunnel, Lynnhaven, Hampton River Inlet,
Hampton Flats, Bluefish Rock, Cape Henry Wreck, Little Creek, Rudee
Inlet, 4th Island Bay Bridge, and Poquoson.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued September 5 at 12:39PM CDT until September 5 at 2:30PM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Central Bottineau County in north central North Dakota...

* WHEN...Until 230 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1239 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Bottineau, Kramer, Gardena and Carbury.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

* WHERE...Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier.

* WHEN...Until Thursday afternoon.

flooding of secondary roads near the river can be expected.

feet on 02/14/2005.
